# package security

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-ieee20305/security"
```

Package security implements the certificate handling of IEEE 2030.5: device identifiers, chain verification for certificates with a HardwareModuleName, and the TLS configurations of clients, servers and notifiers.

IEEE 2030.5 devices and servers authenticate each other with ECDSA P-256 certificates over mutual TLS 1.2. A device is known by identifiers derived from the SHA-256 fingerprint of its certificate: the Long-Form Device Identifier (LFDI) is its leftmost 160 bits (CertificateLFDI), and the Short-Form Device Identifier (SFDI) its leftmost 36 bits as a decimal number followed by a check digit (LFDI.SFDI, SFDI.Valid).

Device certificates of IEEE 2030.5 identify their hardware module in a critical subjectAltName (HardwareModuleName, RFC 4108), which crypto/x509 refuses to verify. Verify verifies such chains, and ClientTLSConfig, ServerTLSConfig and NotificationTLSConfig use it: they never fall back on the system's roots, and a nil pool of roots is ErrConfiguration.

	tlsConfig := security.ServerTLSConfig(serverCert, deviceCAs)
	lfdi := security.CertificateLFDI(r.TLS.PeerCertificates[0])

The cipher suite IEEE 2030.5 mandates, TLS\_ECDHE\_ECDSA\_WITH\_AES\_128\_CCM\_8, is not in crypto/tls: the configurations of this package offer the ECDHE-ECDSA AES-GCM suites, and the module github.com/otfabric/go-ieee20305/tlsccm adds CCM\_8. TestCA, TestServerCert and TestDeviceCert make throwaway certificates for tests and examples.

## Functions

### func ClientTLSConfig

```go
func ClientTLSConfig(device tls.Certificate, roots *x509.CertPool) *tls.Config
```

ClientTLSConfig returns the TLS configuration of an IEEE 2030.5 client: TLS 1.2 or later, the device certificate for mutual TLS, and the CAs that verify the server.

The server's chain is always verified against roots, for server authentication, by Verify in VerifyConnection. The configuration sets InsecureSkipVerify only to turn off the verification of crypto/tls, which rejects the critical subject alternative name that holds the HardwareModuleName of IEEE 2030.5 server certificates. The server name of the connection is checked when the server certificate has DNS names or IP addresses. crypto/tls does not report the server name of a server dialed by IP address, so such a server is identified by its chain alone.

IEEE 2030.5 requires the cipher suite TLS\_ECDHE\_ECDSA\_WITH\_AES\_128\_CCM\_8, which crypto/tls does not implement. Connections use the ECDHE-ECDSA suites crypto/tls offers, which servers commonly accept as well.

### func MarshalHMNSAN

```go
func MarshalHMNSAN(h HMN) ([]byte, error)
```

MarshalHMNSAN returns the DER of a subject alternative name extension value that holds only the HardwareModuleName h.

### func NotificationTLSConfig

```go
func NotificationTLSConfig(server tls.Certificate, deviceCAs *x509.CertPool) *tls.Config
```

NotificationTLSConfig returns the TLS configuration with which a server posts notifications to the listeners of devices: the server certificate as its client certificate, and the listener's chain verified against deviceCAs. A device may serve its listener with its device certificate, whose extended key usage is clientAuth only, so the usage is not checked; the listener's name is, when its certificate has DNS names or IP addresses. As in ClientTLSConfig, InsecureSkipVerify only turns off the verification of crypto/tls, which rejects HardwareModuleName names.

### func ServerTLSConfig

```go
func ServerTLSConfig(server tls.Certificate, clientCAs *x509.CertPool) *tls.Config
```

ServerTLSConfig returns the TLS configuration of an IEEE 2030.5 server: TLS 1.2 or later, the server certificate, and a client certificate that one of clientCAs must have issued for client authentication. The client chain is verified by Verify, which accepts the critical subject alternative name that holds the HardwareModuleName of IEEE 2030.5 device certificates; ConnectionState.VerifiedChains is therefore empty. The chain is verified in VerifyConnection, which crypto/tls also calls on a resumed session: a client certificate that expired since the session was issued is refused then too. See ClientTLSConfig about the cipher suite of IEEE 2030.5.

### func TestCA

```go
func TestCA(org string) (*x509.Certificate, *ecdsa.PrivateKey, error)
```

TestCA generates a self-signed ECDSA P-256 CA certificate and key for testing. The CA is valid for 10 years.

### func TestDeviceCert

```go
func TestDeviceCert(ca *x509.Certificate, caKey *ecdsa.PrivateKey, commonName string) (*x509.Certificate, *ecdsa.PrivateKey, error)
```

TestDeviceCert generates a device (client) certificate signed by the given CA. The certificate is suitable for IEEE 2030.5 mTLS: ECDSA P-256, client auth EKU, 1 year validity.

### func TestDeviceCertHMN

```go
func TestDeviceCertHMN(ca *x509.Certificate, caKey *ecdsa.PrivateKey, h HMN) (*x509.Certificate, *ecdsa.PrivateKey, error)
```

TestDeviceCertHMN generates a device (client) certificate signed by the given CA whose only subject alternative name is the critical HardwareModuleName h, as in IEEE 2030.5 device certificates.

### func TestServerCert

```go
func TestServerCert(ca *x509.Certificate, caKey *ecdsa.PrivateKey, names []string) (*x509.Certificate, *ecdsa.PrivateKey, error)
```

TestServerCert generates a server certificate signed by the given CA. Each name becomes a DNS or, for an IP address literal, an IP subject alternative name; the first is also the common name. The certificate is valid for 1 year.

### func TestServerCertHMN

```go
func TestServerCertHMN(ca *x509.Certificate, caKey *ecdsa.PrivateKey, h HMN) (*x509.Certificate, *ecdsa.PrivateKey, error)
```

TestServerCertHMN generates a server certificate signed by the given CA whose only subject alternative name is the critical HardwareModuleName h, as in IEEE 2030.5 server certificates: it names no host.

### func Verify

```go
func Verify(chain []*x509.Certificate, o VerifyOptions) error
```

Verify verifies the certificate chain of a peer, leaf first, against the roots of o. Unlike x509.Certificate.Verify, it accepts the critical subject alternative name of IEEE 2030.5 certificates when that name holds only RFC 4108 HardwareModuleName otherNames besides DNS names and IP addresses. Every other unhandled critical extension fails verification.

Its errors match ieee20305.ErrCertificate.

### func VerifyPeerCertificate

```go
func VerifyPeerCertificate(o VerifyOptions) func(rawCerts [][]byte, _ [][]*x509.Certificate) error
```

VerifyPeerCertificate returns a tls.Config.VerifyPeerCertificate callback that parses the peer's certificates and verifies them with Verify.

## Types

### type HMN

```go
type HMN struct {
	Type         asn1.ObjectIdentifier
	SerialNumber []byte
}
```

HMN is an RFC 4108 HardwareModuleName: the type of a hardware module and its serial number. IEEE 2030.5 device and server certificates carry one as an otherName of their subject alternative name.

#### func HardwareModuleName

```go
func HardwareModuleName(c *x509.Certificate) (HMN, bool)
```

HardwareModuleName returns the first RFC 4108 HardwareModuleName in the subject alternative name of c, and whether c has one.

#### func (HMN) Equal

```go
func (h HMN) Equal(o HMN) bool
```

Equal reports whether h and o name the same hardware module.

### type LFDI

```go
type LFDI [20]byte
```

LFDI is a Long-Form Device Identifier: the leftmost 160 bits (20 bytes) of the SHA-256 fingerprint of a DER-encoded certificate, represented as 40 uppercase hex characters.

#### func CertificateLFDI

```go
func CertificateLFDI(cert *x509.Certificate) LFDI
```

CertificateLFDI derives the LFDI from a parsed certificate.

#### func DERBytesLFDI

```go
func DERBytesLFDI(der []byte) LFDI
```

DERBytesLFDI derives the LFDI from DER-encoded certificate bytes.

#### func ParseLFDI

```go
func ParseLFDI(s string) (LFDI, error)
```

ParseLFDI parses a 40-character hex string into an LFDI.

#### func (LFDI) SFDI

```go
func (l LFDI) SFDI() SFDI
```

SFDI derives the Short-Form Device Identifier from this LFDI.

#### func (LFDI) String

```go
func (l LFDI) String() string
```

String returns the LFDI as a 40-character uppercase hex string.

### type SFDI

```go
type SFDI uint64
```

SFDI is a Short-Form Device Identifier: the leftmost 36 bits of the SHA-256 fingerprint as a decimal number, followed by a check digit that makes the sum of all its digits a multiple of 10 (at most 12 digits).

#### func (SFDI) String

```go
func (s SFDI) String() string
```

String returns the SFDI as a decimal string.

#### func (SFDI) Valid

```go
func (s SFDI) Valid() bool
```

Valid reports whether the SFDI's check digit is correct.

### type VerifyOptions

```go
type VerifyOptions struct {
	// Roots are the trusted CAs: the CAs of the IEEE 2030.5 PKI. Required:
	// a nil pool fails verification rather than falling back to the
	// system roots, which would let any publicly trusted certificate in.
	Roots *x509.CertPool
	// Intermediates are CAs that may complete the chain besides the
	// certificates that follow the leaf in the chain itself.
	Intermediates *x509.CertPool
	// ServerName is the expected host name or IP address of the peer. It
	// is checked only when the leaf has DNS or IP subject alternative
	// names; certificates that name only a hardware module are identified
	// by their chain and PinnedLFDI.
	ServerName string
	// PinnedLFDI, when set, is the LFDI the leaf must have.
	PinnedLFDI *LFDI
	// Usage is the extended key usage the chain must allow. Zero
	// (x509.ExtKeyUsageAny) accepts any usage.
	Usage x509.ExtKeyUsage
	// Now returns the time to verify at. Nil uses time.Now.
	Now func() time.Time
}
```

VerifyOptions are the options of Verify.
